walkthrough: Goal: find a brush by the job I do with it instead of in one long list, keep the brushes I use together and in my order, and get back to the brush I just drew with.

Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape) on an empty library; a blank artwork opens with the Ink Pen. Tap the Brush button: the Brushes panel opens. Under its heading the sets as words in two columns: Recent and Sketching, Inking and Painting, Texture. Inking, which holds the Ink Pen, is in the ink pill; the list under the words shows Ink Pen (outlined: chosen), Inker and Monoline with their strokes, then StreamLine as before.
Recent before anything is drawn: tap Recent: the pill slides there, and the list says 'Brushes you draw with appear here.' in the quiet grey hint.
Draw: a pen stroke on the canvas outside the panel closes it and draws a line with the Ink Pen.

Another set: tap the Brush button: the panel opens on Inking again (it always opens on the chosen brush's set, never on Recent). Tap Texture: the pill slides there, the list shows Textured Round and Speckle. Tap Speckle: it is outlined, chosen. Draw a stroke on the canvas: a spray of dots.

Recent: tap the Brush button: the panel opens on Texture, Speckle outlined. Tap Recent: Speckle, then Ink Pen, newest first. A tap there would choose the brush; holding a row lifts nothing: Recent is never arranged by hand.

Arrange: tap Texture, press and hold Speckle: after a moment its row lifts (paper and an ink outline, as a layer row does) and follows the finger; dragged above Textured Round, Textured Round slides down to make room; let go: Speckle lies first. Letting a row go where it lay changes nothing.

Another set for a brush: tap Speckle (it is chosen): its editor opens in the panel; under its name a row 'Set' with Sketching, Inking, Painting and Texture as words, Texture in the pill, then the preview strip. Tap Painting: the pill slides there. Back: the list shows Painting, which now ends with Speckle, still chosen; tap Texture: only Textured Round.
A copy: tap Painting, tap Speckle, then Duplicate in its editor: the editor shows 'Speckle copy', chosen; Back: Painting lists Speckle copy right after Speckle.
Undo and failure: arranging brushes is no step of the artwork, as editing them is not: undo takes back strokes only. Nothing here can fail; a set emptied by hand simply lists nothing.

Reopen: leave the app and come back: the canvas as it was; the Brush button opens Painting with Speckle and Speckle copy at its end, the copy chosen; Texture holds Textured Round alone; Recent lists Speckle and Ink Pen.
Other tools: tap Eraser, then Eraser again: its picker shows the same sets, opening on Inking, where its own brush, the Ink Pen, lies; Painting there ends with Speckle and Speckle copy too.
